bib.title: LongLoRA: Efficient Fine-tuning of Long-Context Large Language Models

question: Can the context window of pre-trained LLMs be extended cheaply, with sparse shifted attention during fine-tuning and a LoRA variant, while keeping full attention at inference?
hypothesis: Short (grouped) attention with shifting approximates long-context attention during training, and LoRA closes the gap to full fine-tuning if embedding and normalization layers are trainable.
contributions: Shifted sparse attention (S2-Attn), two lines of code, training only
LoRA+ : LoRA plus trainable embedding and normalization layers
Extend Llama2 7B to 100k, 13B to 65536, 70B to 32768 on one 8x A100 machine

method.summary: Fine-tune Llama2 with Position Interpolation and S2-Attn (half the heads shifted by half a group, group = 1/4 of context) plus LoRA with trainable embeddings and norms, on RedPajama by next-token prediction; inference uses standard full attention. Also SFT on LongAlpaca-12k.
method.task: long-context extension of pre-trained LLMs (perplexity, retrieval)

datasets.name: LongAlpaca-12k
datasets.size: 12k: 9k long-context QA + 3k short QA sampled from Alpaca
datasets.source: self-collected from technical papers, science fiction, books

training.warmup: linear learning rate warmup (length not stated)
training.hardware: single 8x A100 machine; DeepSpeed stage 2 (stage 3 for max context), Flash-Attention2, gradient checkpointing

other.LoRA rank: 8 in Table 2 headline; not otherwise stated
other.SFT: same lr, weight decay, batch size as extension step, 5 epochs

inference.prompting: SFT prompt: Below is {material type}. Memorize the content and answer my question after the paper. {material content} Now the material ends. {question}

metrics.name: perplexity
metrics.definition: sliding window S=256 on PG19 / proof-pile

eval.protocol: single runs, no seeds or significance reported

results.claim: S2-Attn full fine-tuning at 32768 target context reaches PPL 8.08 vs full attention 8.04, while short attention without shift reaches 9.47
results.setup: Llama2 7B fully fine-tuned on RedPajama, target context 32768, S2-Attn group size 1/4 of target

results.claim: With S2-Attn at 32768, plain LoRA at rank 8 is far behind full FT; larger rank does not close the gap
results.setup: Llama2 7B, S2-Attn, RedPajama, target 32768; LoRA rank 8 to 256 gives 11.44 to 11.98
results.table: Table 2, row PPL, column LoRA rank 8

results.claim: Making normalization and embedding layers trainable (LoRA+) closes the LoRA gap
results.setup: Llama2 7B, S2-Attn, target 32768, LoRA rank 8 + Norm & Embed
results.table: Table 2, row PPL, column + Norm & Embed

results.claim: Normalization layers are 0.004% of Llama2 7B parameters
results.quote: Especially for normal- ization layers, the parameters are only 0.004% in the whole Llama2 7B.

results.claim: Perplexity improves with longer evaluation context for 7B trained at 32768 (proof-pile, LoRA+ with S2-Attn)
results.setup: Llama2 7B trained at 32768 with S2-Attn + LoRA+, evaluated at 32768 context; 8192-trained model gives 2.72 at 8192
results.note: Text: perplexity gets better from 2.72 to 2.50 by -0.22

results.claim: LongLoRA extends Llama2 7B to 100k, 13B to 65536, 70B to 32768 on a single 8x A100 machine; 7B at 100k evaluates at 2.52 on proof-pile at 100,000 context
results.setup: Llama2 7B trained at 100,000 context, DeepSpeed stage 3, evaluated at 100,000

results.claim: Training time at 65536 context: LongLoRA 52.4 h vs LoRA 92.5 h; Full FT OOM
results.setup: Llama2 7B, 1000 iterations, 8x A100, Flash-Attention2, DeepSpeed stage 2, per-GPU batch 1, grad accum 8
results.table: Table 12, row LongLoRA, column 65536 Train hours
results.note: Text: LongLoRA spends 56.6% of LoRA training hours at 65536

results.claim: Without Flash-Attention2, S2-Attn gives 2.1x training speedup and 1.8x memory saving at 8192 context
results.baseline_value: 17.5 h w/o vs 8.2 h with S2-Attn
results.quote: Without Flash-Attention2 (Dao, 2023), S2-Attn improves the training speed by 2.1× and GPU memory cost by 1.8× on 8192 context length.

results.claim: Attention share of FLOPs rises from 24.5% at 8192 to 72.2% at 65536, falling to 39.4% with S2-Attn
results.quote: Attn has 24.5% of the total FLOPs at the 8192 context length while it increases to 72.2% at the 65536 context length. It decreases to 39.4% when S2-Attn is used.

results.claim: Topic retrieval on LongChat at 16k: Ours-13B 0.94 vs LongChat-13B 0.9
results.setup: Llama2 13B fine-tuned at 18k context on RedPajama next-token; LongChat topic retrieval

results.claim: Passkey retrieval: model fine-tuned on 32768 shows no accuracy degradation until 33k or 34k; extended PI to 48k gives 60%-90% in 33k-45k
results.setup: Llama2 7B fine-tuned at 32768, tested 1k to 34k at ~1k interval, 10 random passkeys each
results.quote: presents moderate retrieval ability (60%-90% accuracy) in the range of 33k to 45k

results.claim: S2-Attn pattern ablation: with full attention at test, S2-Attn cro. heads gets 8.12 while stride sparse gets 24.03
results.baseline_value: Full-Attn row 8.64 (sparse test) ... see table; stride sparse 24.03
results.setup: Llama2 7B to 32768, improved LoRA, tested with full attention
results.table: Table 6, row test w/ full-attn, column S2-Attn cro. heads

results.claim: Group size 1/2 and 1/4 of context give minor gaps to full attention; smaller groups are worse
LongBench average: Ours-7B 36.8 vs GPT-3.5-Turbo 44.0 and LongChat-v1.5-7B 34.3
results.setup: Llama2 7B SFT at 16384 context on LongAlpaca-12k, about 4 hours, 0.3B tokens

limits: Perplexity degrades on short contexts after extension, a known Position Interpolation limitation (Sec 4.2)
LoRA rank, alpha, LR schedule, warmup length, precision and seeds not stated
Only Llama2 and RoPE position interpolation tested; authors plan other LLMs and position encodings
Peak memory barely differs from LoRA with Flash-Attention2; gain is mainly training time
Mostly perplexity and retrieval evaluation; SFT evaluated only on LongBench/LEval at 7B
Shifting moves last tokens to the front group, inconsistent with causal masks, though ablated (Table 8) to no effect
